extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students and researchers studying enumerative combinatorics and poset/arrangement theory
extracted.subtask_description: Work through textbook-style exercises about lattices, posets, M"obius functions, hyperplane arrangements, chromatic polynomials, and related enumerative/combinatorial structures; prove stated propositions, compute invariants, and derive identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interval is Boolean algebra when µ(s,t)=±1
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that if µ(s, t) = ±1, then the interval [s, t] is a boolean algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (original wording: “Show that if µ(s, t) = 1, then the interval [s, t] is a boolean algebra.”)

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite classification of geometric lattices with given µ
rubrics_metrics.description: Let n ∈ P. Show that there exist finitely many geometric lattices L1, . . . , Lk such that if L is any finite geometric lattice satisfying µ(ˆ0, ˆ1) | µ(ˆ0, ˆ1) = n, then L ∼= Li × Bd for some i and d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–]* (show existence of finitely many building-block geometric lattices producing given value of µ at top)

rubrics_metrics.name: Injective map between subsets in finite lattice (existence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be a finite lattice and A, B subsets of L. Suppose that for all t in L there exists t* > t such that µ(t, t*) = 0. Show that there exists an injective map φ : B → A satisfying φ(s) ≥ s whenever u ∈ A implies u ∈ B. (Thus ... )
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3] (construct an injective map using the given µ-vanishing property; text contains additional conditions/hint)

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular lattice consequences: geometric lattice and atom/coatom counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K be a finite modular lattice. Show: (i) If ˆ1 is a join of atoms of K, then K is a geometric lattice and hence µ(ˆ0,ˆ1) = 0. (ii) With K as in (i), K has the same number of atoms as coatoms. (iii) For any a, b in K, define the map ψ_b on intervals; show it is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (three-part statement about modular lattices; follow modular/duality arguments)

rubrics_metrics.name: Injective map between Jk and Mk in finite modular lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Let J_k be elements that cover at most k elements and M_k elements that are covered by at most k elements. Deduce existence of an injective map φ : J_k → M_k satisfying φ(s) ≥ s for all s in J_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (deduce from previous parts (a) and (b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of counts of elements covering vs covered by k elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that in a finite modular lattice L the number of elements covering exactly k elements equals the number of elements covered by exactly k elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2–] (consequence of injective maps between Jk and Mk)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pk and Rk need not be isomorphic
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Pk be subposet of elements of L that cover k elements and Rk the subposet of elements that are covered by k elements. Show by example that we need not have Pk ∼= Rk (unlike distributive lattices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (provide explicit counterexample)

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduce earlier exercise from injectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce Exercise 3.96(d) from the injectivity result in part (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (use established maps to infer previous exercise)

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of join-irreducible with small dual order ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be a finite lattice with n elements. Does there exist a join-irreducible t of L such that the principal dual order ideal V_t := { s ∈ L : s ≥ t } has at most n/2 elements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (yes/no question; produce proof or counterexample)

rubrics_metrics.name: Large dual order ideal forces µ vanishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be any finite lattice with n elements. Suppose that there is a t ≠ ˆ0 in L such that #V_t > n/2. Show that µ(ˆ0, s) = 0 for some s in L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (use combinatorial/Möbius arguments)

rubrics_metrics.name: µ(ˆ0,ˆ1) bounds for lattices with antichain S intersecting every maximal chain
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be a finite lattice containing a subset S of cardinality n that is an antichain and every maximal chain of L meets S. Find, as a function of n, the smallest and largest possible values of µ(ˆ0,ˆ1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3] (determine extremal possible Möbius values; show examples for n=2,3)

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum possible µ(ˆ0,ˆ1) for small posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be an (n + 2)-element poset with ˆ0 and ˆ1. What is the largest possible value of µ(ˆ0,ˆ1)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (exercise asks for extremal value)

rubrics_metrics.name: Largest µ(ˆ0,ˆ1) for n-element lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: Same question as previous but for n-element lattices L: find largest possible µ(ˆ0,ˆ1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [5] (lattice-specific extremal problem)

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximise |µ(ˆ0,ˆ1)| with degree and cover bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k, ℓ be integers. Over all finite posets P with ˆ0 and ˆ1 and longest chain of length ℓ, such that every element of P is covered by at most k elements, find max_P |µ(ˆ0,ˆ1)|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [5–] (optimization over poset family)

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisibility properties and presence of 5-element sublattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be a finite lattice for which |µ_L(ˆ0,ˆ1)| ≥ 101. Suppose L contains an order ideal I of the boolean algebra B_n of rank at most k. Show divisibility properties of #I (e.g., divisible by 2^{2k+1} or similar) and discuss whether L must contain a sublattice isomorphic to 1⊕1⊕1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (fragmented original; show stated divisibility and structural consequences)

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph chromatic polynomial via stable partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G be a graph with vertex set V of size p. Define SG(k) as number of stable (independent) partitions of V with k blocks. Show χ_G(n) = Σ_j SG(j) (n)_j (umbral form) and deduce χ_G(n) is a monic polynomial of degree p with integer coefficients and the coefficient of n^{p-1} is −#E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2–]* (establish combinatorial expansion of chromatic polynomial; note coefficient information)

rubrics_metrics.name: Chromatic polynomial via connected partition lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L_G be the poset of partitions of V whose blocks are connected (ordered by refinement). Show χ_G(n) = Σ_{π∈L_G} µ(ˆ0,π) n^{#π} and deduce χ_G(n) = n^c χ_{L_G}(n) where c is number of connected components of G. Verify special case for complete graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (relate graph and arrangement characteristic polynomials)

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical arrangement and intersection lattice isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Let B_G be the hyperplane arrangement in R^p with hyperplanes x_i = x_j for edges ij ∈ E. Show that L_G ≅ L(B_G) (intersection lattice of B_G) and deduce χ_G = χ_{B_G}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (establish isomorphism between partition poset and intersection lattice)

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion-contraction recurrence for chromatic polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Let e be an edge of G. Prove χ_G(n) = χ_{G-e}(n) − χ_{G/e}(n) and give a direct combinatorial proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (use graphical arrangement viewpoint or combinatorial coloring argument)

rubrics_metrics.name: Umbral mapping of chromatic polynomial to stable-partition generating function
rubrics_metrics.description: Let φ: Q[n] → Q[x] be defined by φ(n^k) = Σ_j S(k,j) x^j. Show φ(χ_G(n)) = Σ_j S_G(j) x^j, where S_G(j) counts stable partitions of size j. Deduce umbral identity χ_G(B) = B_G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (connect chromatic polynomial under linear transform to stable partition generating polynomial)

rubrics_metrics.name: Acyclic orientations enumerated by chromatic polynomial at −1
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove ao(G) = (−1)^p χ_G(−1), where ao(G) is the number of acyclic orientations of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (use deletion-contraction or Theorem 3.11.7)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regions of arrangement determined by inversion set of permutation
rubrics_metrics.description: Let w ∈ S_n and A_w be arrangement of hyperplanes x_i = x_j for all inversions (i,j) of w. Show r(A_w) ≥ #Λ_w where Λ_w is principal order ideal of w in Bruhat order; equality holds iff w avoids patterns 4231, 35142, 42513, 351624.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3] (relate number of regions to Bruhat order principal ideal and pattern avoidance)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regions of Shi arrangement count
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a bijective proof that the number of regions of the Shi arrangement in S_n is (n+1)^{n-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (construct explicit bijection)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponential sequences of arrangements (ESA) conditions and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Define exponential sequence of arrangements (ESA) with conditions A1, A2, A3; show braid arrangements and Shi arrangements form ESAs, and derive related generating-function identities connecting characteristic polynomials and exponential generating functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [1+]*, [3–], [3–] (establish ESA structure and deduce generating-function relations)

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-field method proof of Deletion-Restriction recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the finite-field method (Theorem 3.11.10) to give a proof of the Deletion-Restriction recurrence for arrangements defined over Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (apply finite-field point-counting technique)

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic polynomials for specific arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: For several listed arrangements in R^n (e.g., full braid with coordinate hyperplanes, etc.) show the characteristic polynomials equal specified products (formulas given in exercises 114–116).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2–] to [3–] (compute characteristic polynomials by known techniques; multiple specific instances)

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic polynomial of perpendicular-bisector arrangement for generic points
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v1,...,vk be generic points in R^n and C(v1,...,vk) the arrangement of perpendicular bisectors of all pairs; find characteristic polynomial χ_C and number of regions r(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (use geometry and intersection-lattice analysis)

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderings of spacelike events via signless Stirling numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Given k spacelike events in (n+1)-dimensional Minkowski space occurring in order in one frame, determine the number of different event orders observers in other inertial frames can see; express answer using signless Stirling numbers c(n,i) of first kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (use Lorentz transformation and combinatorial enumeration)

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeness of module of derivations and characteristic polynomial factorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a linear hyperplane arrangement in R^d and Ω its corresponding module of polynomial vector fields. If Ω is a free R-module with homogeneous generators of degrees e_i, show χ_{L(A)}(x) = Π_{i=1}^r (x − e_i). Also: show Ω free when L is supersolvable, give examples, and discuss whether freeness depends only on intersection lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3+], [3], [3], [5] (link algebraic freeness to factorization of characteristic polynomials; include counterexamples and dependence issues)

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting injective linear maps via Möbius inversion on subspace lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V be n-dimensional over F_q and X a space over F_q with x vectors. Count injective linear transformations V→X in two ways (direct and by Möbius inversion on lattice of subspaces) to derive a polynomial identity equivalent to the q-binomial theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (two-count method producing polynomial identity)

rubrics_metrics.name: q-analogue conditions for graded posets (binomial-coefficient counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be finite graded poset of rank n and q≥2. Show two equivalent conditions: (1) For every interval [s,t] of length k we have µ(s,t) = (−1)^k q^{(k choose 2)}; (2) for every interval [s,t] of length k and all 0≤i≤k the number of elements of rank i in [s,t] equals the q-binomial coefficient evaluated at q. Ask whether for large n such posets must be B_n(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–], [5–] (establish equivalence and investigate uniqueness/classification)

rubrics_metrics.name: Möbius function for posets forbidding k consecutive integers
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix k≥2. Let L'_n be poset of subsets of [n] with no k consecutive integers, adjoin ˆ1 to form L_n. Let µ_n denote Möbius function of L_n. Find µ_n(∅,ˆ1) depending only on n modulo 2k+2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (periodicity-modular classification)

rubrics_metrics.name: Möbius function of unitary-divisor poset and analogue of inversion formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Let poset L be positive integers ordered by unitary divisibility. Describe the Möbius function of L and state unitary analogue of classical Möbius inversion formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (number-theoretic poset Möbius description)

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervals in monoid-with-commuting-generators are distributive lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M be a monoid generated by g1,...,gn with relations g_i g_j = g_j g_i for certain commuting pairs. Show any interval [ε,w] in M is a distributive lattice L_w and describe poset P_w with L_w = J(P_w). Deduce number of factorizations equals number e(P_w) of linear extensions, and derive Möbius function formula for M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (combinatorial description of factorization lattices; provide explicit Möbius formula)

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating function identity for element counts in the monoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Let N(a1,...,an) be number of distinct elements of M of degree Σ a_i in generators g_i. Deduce generating-function identity Σ N(a1,...,an) x1^{a1}...xn^{an} = Σ_{r≥0} (−1)^r Σ_{i1<...<ir, commuting} x_{i1}...x_{ir} / Π_{i=1}^n (1−x_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (use Möbius function result to obtain generating function; consider extreme commuting/noncommuting cases)

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic polynomial of supersolvable semimodular lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be finite supersolvable semimodular lattice with M-chain with atom counts a_i between successive chain elements. Show χ_L(q) = Π_{i=1}^n (q − a_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (use structure of supersolvable lattices and factorization theorem)

rubrics_metrics.name: R-labelable poset LP construction and equality of β invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Given natural partial order P and lattice L, define LP = { t ∈ L : Λ(t) ∈ J(P) } and show LP is R-labelable and β_{LP}(S) = β_L(S) (Jordan–Hölder set equality). Note dependence on choice of chain/linear extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (construct LP and compare β-invariants)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterization of supersolvable lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Show for a finite graded lattice L of rank n that L is supersolvable iff L has an R-labeling for which the label of every maximal chain is a permutation of 1,2,...,n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (equivalence between structural and labeling properties)

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and enumeration for posets L_k(p) from subgroup lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix prime p and k≥1. Define posets L^{(1)}_k(p), L^{(2)}_k(p), L^{(3)}_k(p) corresponding to subgroup lattices of Z^k of finite index, finite subgroups of (Z/p^∞Z)^k, and subgroups of (Z/p^n Z)^k. Show isomorphism L^{(1)}_k(p) ∼= L^{(3)}_k(p), deduce local finiteness and rank generating function F(L_k(p),x) = Π_{i=0}^{k-1} 1/ (1− p^{i} x), and compute α and β values using q-binomial coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] to [3–] (algebraic/combinatorial analysis; several subparts)

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting maximal chains and orbits in partition lattice Π_n
rubrics_metrics.description: How many maximal chains does Π_n have? Show the symmetric group S_n acting on Π_n induces M = En / S_n orbits on maximal chains and relate to Euler numbers; analyze subposet Λ_n with specified singleton-block rule, count maximal chains and show supersolvability and β_Λn(S) properties; interpret β_Λn(S) combinatorially in terms of alternating permutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2–] to [5–] (enumeration and representation-theoretic orbit-counting; combinatorial interpretations)

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting in poset of permutations with type conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π of Π_n of type (a1,a2,...), and σ satisfying π∨σ = ˆ1 and π∧σ = ˆ0, compute f(π) the number of σ of this property and show specified product formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–]* (counting compatible complements in partition lattice)

rubrics_metrics.name: Congruence property of Möbius number under fixed-point-free automorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be finite poset with fixed-point-free automorphism σ of prime order p. Show µ_P(ˆ0,ˆ1) ≡ −1 (mod p). Apply to P = Π_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (use orbit-stabilizer and automorphism action on chains)

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform posets: matrix inversion relations and classification question
rubrics_metrics.description: Define uniform poset P (intervals [t,ˆ1] isomorphic to fixed Qi depending on rank). Show matrices V(i,j) and v(i,j) are inverses, and ask to find interesting uniform posets and classify uniform geometric lattices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+], [5] (linear-algebraic relations between Whitney numbers; classification open-ended)

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial G-partitions poset Q_n(G) properties and characteristic polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Q_n(G) as poset of equivalence classes of partial G-partitions. Show Q_n(G) ≅ Π_{n+1} when |G|=1, show Q_n(G) is supersolvable geometric lattice of rank n, and compute χ_{Q_n(G)}(t) = Π_{i=1}^n (t − m i) where m = |G|. Show Q_n(G) is uniform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2–] to [3–] (construction and characteristic polynomial derivation)

rubrics_metrics.name: Poset P_n defined by odd-indexed subsets: enumerative invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Define P_n as family of certain subsets of {1,...,2n+1} with odd-index conditions. Compute number of elements of rank k, total number, Möbius µ(ˆ0,ˆ1), number of maximal chains, and interval factorization properties. Show P_n^* is uniform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (explicit combinatorial enumeration and structural isomorphisms)

rubrics_metrics.name: Möbius function properties in subgroup lattice of S_n
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L_n be lattice of subgroups of S_n with Möbius function µ_n. (a) Show Σ_{G transitive} µ_n(ˆ0,G) = (−1)^{n−1} (n−1)!. (b) Show µ_n(ˆ0,ˆ1) divisible by n!/2. (c)-(f) Refine formula via transitive proper subgroups containing odd involution and deduce explicit values for prime n, n=2^a, and n=2p (p odd prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] to [3–] (group-theoretic Möbius summations and divisibility conclusions)

rubrics_metrics.name: Möbius function in subword and factor orders on free monoid
rubrics_metrics.description: For subword order on A^* show µ(u,v) = (−1)^{ℓ(v)−ℓ(u)} s(u,v) where s(u,v) counts subwords using all special letters. For factor order give recursive determination of µ(u,v) via longest proper prefix/suffix factors ι_v and ϕ_v with explicit cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–]* (use Philip Hall sign-reversing involution or recursive combinatorics)

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition refinement poset Λ_n of integer partitions: Möbius and CM properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Λ_n be integer partitions of n ordered by refinement. Show Λ_n is graded of rank n−1, determine Möbius function µ(λ,ρ), and decide whether µ alternates in sign and whether Λ_n is Cohen–Macaulay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2–] to [5] (structural and homological properties of partition refinement poset)

rubrics_metrics.name: Möbius function under dominance order on partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Λ_n be partitions of n ordered by dominance. Determine µ for this ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3] (compare with refinement order; different partial order causes different Möbius)

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeta polynomial relations for disjoint union and product of posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Express zeta polynomial values Z(P + Q, m) and Z(P × Q, m) in terms of Z(P, j) and Z(Q, j) for suitable j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (combinatorial convolution/product relations)

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeta polynomial of poset of intervals Int(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be finite poset and Int(P) poset of nonempty intervals ordered by inclusion. Relate Z(P,n) and Z(Int(P),n). If P has ˆ0 and ˆ1 and Q = Int(P) with ˆ0 adjoined relate µ_P(ˆ0,ˆ1) and µ_Q(ˆ0,ˆ1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (explicit relationships via interval decomposition)

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeta polynomial generating function for ordinal-sum-of-antichains Uk
rubrics_metrics.description: Let U_k be ordinal sum of k 2-element antichains (#U_k = 2k). Show Z(U_k,n) x^k = Σ_{k≥0} (1/2) (1 + x/n)^{n} (?) [original formula provided].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (derive generating-function identity given in exercise)

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear map φ on polynomials maps zeta polynomials to chain-count polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Let φ: Q[n] → Q[x] be linear map taking n^k to Σ_j j! S(k,j) x^j. Show φ(Z(P, n + 2)) = Σ_j c_j(P) x^j where c_j(P) is # of j-element chains of P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (use Stirling-number expansions and combinatorial interpretations)

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations between zeta polynomials and chain-poset ch(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Q = ch(P) poset of nonempty chains of P. Show relations among Z(P,m+1), Z(Q_0,m+1), Möbius numbers b_Q(ˆ0,ˆ1), and express b_P(ˆ0,ˆ1) in terms of chain-count coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (several connected subparts relating chain poset zeta and Möbius invariants)

rubrics_metrics.name: Eulerian poset reciprocal identity for Fn(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q is Eulerian, show Fn(x) = (−1)^n Fn(−x/(1+x)) where Fn(x) = Σ_{k=1}^n k! S(n,k) x^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2–] (use Stirling numbers and Eulerian properties)

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitionability, R-labelability and Cohen–Macaulay question
rubrics_metrics.description: Define chain-partitionable (partitionable) poset and show R-labelable implies partitionable. Ask whether every Cohen–Macaulay poset is partitionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] to [5] (structural implications and open-ended question)

rubrics_metrics.name: Order polynomial depends only on comparability graph
rubrics_metrics.description: Show order polynomial Ω_P(m) depends only on the comparability graph Com(P), i.e., if two posets have same comparability graph they have same order polynomial. Provide example where Com(P) not isomorphic but order polynomials equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–], [2] (graph-theoretic dependence and counterexample)

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between order polynomials for boolean algebras of successive ranks
rubrics_metrics.description: Show Ω_{B_{n+1}}(2) = Ω_{B_n}(3), where B_k is boolean algebra of rank k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2]* (evaluate order polynomials at small integers and relate)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity theorem for order polynomials via J(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Ω_P(n) = Z(J(P), n). Use Example 3.9.6 to give another proof of the reciprocity theorem for order polynomials (Theorem 3.15.10) in case of natural labelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (connect distributive-lattice zeta polynomials to reciprocity)

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit order polynomial values for chain and antichain
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Ω_P(n) and (−1)^p Ω_P(−n) explicitly when (i) P is a p-element chain, and (ii) P is a p-element antichain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [1+] (straightforward explicit formulas)

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeta polynomial for lattices of faces of Platonic solids
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Z(L,n) when L is lattice of faces of each of the five Platonic solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [1+] (explicit computation by face-lattice enumeration)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum over labelings of order polynomial values
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ω range over all p! labelings of P. Find simple expression for Σ_ω Ω_{P,ω}(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2]* (sum over all labelings simplifies; provide explicit formula)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinantal formula for zeta polynomial in Young's lattice interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix µ ≤ λ in Young's lattice Y and set Z(n) = ζ^n(µ,λ). Choose r so λ_{r+1}=0 and show Z(n+1) equals determinant with entries combinatorial binomial terms (explicit determinant formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3] (use hook/Young tableau combinatorics and determinant identities)

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating functions counting chains in Young's lattice and q-analogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Given S = {a1,...,aj} subset and chains λ_0<... in Young's lattice define f_S(n) and show generating function relations: f_S(n) q^n = P(q) A_S(q) with A_S(q) rational with denominator φ_{a_j}(q), compute special cases and deduce identities involving β_Y(S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] to [3–] (q-analogue enumerations using generating-function techniques)

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicial complex of linear extensions and homology of Δ_P
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite naturally labeled poset P construct simplicial complex Δ_P whose faces are linear extensions of P, with face dimension des(w). For P a p-element antichain draw Δ_P and compute reduced homology H_i(Δ_P;Z) vanishing ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] to [3] (explicit construction and homological computations)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower bound on number of linear extensions with βJ(P)(S)>0
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p-element poset P and S ⊆ [p−1] with β_{J(P)}(S) > 0. What is least number of linear extensions P can have?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (minimization problem conditioned on nonzero β-invariant)

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishability of distributive lattices by β-invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: If L and L' are distributive lattices of rank n with β_L(S)=β_{L'}(S) for all S ⊆ [n−1], are L and L' isomorphic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (determine whether β-vector determines the distributive lattice)

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-dual intervals imply αP(S) depends only on multiset of gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P finite graded poset of rank n such that every interval is self-dual. Show α_P(S) depends only on multiset of numbers n1,n2−n1,... (the gaps) and not their order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (use self-duality to deduce invariance under permutation of rank-gaps)

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize finite distributive lattices with all intervals self-dual
rubrics_metrics.description: Show a finite distributive lattice in which every interval is self-dual must be a product of chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2]* (structural classification)

rubrics_metrics.name: α and β for infinite poset N^N
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P = N^N and S finite multiset m1<m2<...⊂P. Define α_P(S) and β_P(S) as in Section 3.13 and show explicit product formula β_N^N(S) = m1(m2−m1−1)...(ms−ms−1−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (extend finite definitions to certain infinite posets)

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations expressing characteristic polynomial by β_k values
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be finite graded poset rank n. Show Δ^{k+1} Z(P,0) = Σ_{|S|=k} α_P(S) and express generating function Σ β_k x^{k+1}/(1−x)^{n+1} etc. Derive χ_P(q) in terms of β_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (algebraic relations connecting zeta polynomial differences, α/β invariants, and characteristic polynomial)

rubrics_metrics.name: Poset P_{k,t} of block-size divisible partitions: zeta polynomial and Catalan connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P_{k,t} be poset of partitions of [kt] with block sizes divisible by k and no interleaving condition. Show Z(P_{k,t}, n+1) = ((kn+1)^t)/t!, deduce Catalan enumerations and structural isomorphism P_{2,t} ≅ Int(P_{1,t}), count maximal chains, and give formulas for number of elements of given type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [3–] (semantics and enumerations linking to Catalan numbers and interval poset structures)

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute order on symmetric group and interval isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Define absolute order A(S_n) on S_n by u⋖v if v=(i,j)u and #cycles decreases by 1. Show that for w an n-cycle, [ˆ0,w] ≅ P_{1,n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (combinatorial isomorphism between permutation intervals and partition posets)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence classes of labelings and acyclic orientations count
rubrics_metrics.description: Define two labelings ω,ω' of a p-element poset P equivalent if (P,ω)=(P,ω'). Show number of equivalence classes equals number of acyclic orientations of Hasse diagram of P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (connect labeling equivalence to acyclic orientations enumeration)

rubrics_metrics.name: Shuffle sets enumeration depends only on descent sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix u of length j and v of length k on disjoint integer sets. For w a shuffle of u and v, show number of shuffles with descent set S depends only on D(u) and D(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2] (use (P,ω)-partition theory)

rubrics_metrics.name: Product formula for W-polynomial under disjoint union of posets
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P1,P2 disjoint posets with labelings; show W_{P1+P2,ω}(x) = binomial(p1+p2,p1)^{-1} W_{P1,ω1}(x) W_{P2,ω2}(x) where p_i = #P_i (explicit combinatorial product relation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [2+] (convolution/product identity for W-polynomials; final formula given in exercise)
